scenes.scene: Medium-wide shot at eye level of three people standing apart from each other. Setting: Babuji's small room at night in an old North Indian village house: whitewashed walls with damp patches, an old iron bed with a thin cotton mattress against the back wall, a wooden shelf with a few brass pots, a hanging lantern giving warm amber light, a green tin trunk with a big iron padlock on the floor in the middle of the room. On the LEFT of the frame: Vikram (a 42-year-old Indian man: sharp oval face with a straight nose and a clean-shaven chin, intelligent dark-brown eyes behind thin rimless glasses, fair wheatish skin, short neat black hair greying at the temples, a fit slim build, about 5 feet 10 inches tall; wearing a navy-blue formal shirt with rolled sleeves and grey trousers), body and face turned towards the right of the frame, eyes on Sunny the whole time; sits on a low wooden stool beside the trunk, tired, guarded. In the BACKGROUND: Savitri (Amma) (a 64-year-old Indian woman: gentle oval face with deep wrinkles around the eyes, soft kind dark-brown eyes, wheatish-brown skin, grey hair parted in the middle and tied in a low bun, a small slightly stooped build, about 5 feet 1 inch tall; wearing a plain white cotton widow's saree with a grey woollen shawl), turned three-quarters towards the camera, angled to the left of the frame, eyes on Vikram the whole time; sits on the edge of the iron bed, hands folded, grieving, quiet. On the RIGHT of the frame: Sunny (a 34-year-old Indian man: round friendly face with a short thick black beard, bright dark-brown eyes, sun-darkened brown skin, thick wavy black hair, broad shoulders and strong arms, a sturdy build, about 5 feet 8 inches tall; wearing a faded brown kurta with rolled sleeves and grease stains), body and face turned towards the left of the frame, eyes on Vikram the whole time; sits on the floor against the wall, arms on his knees, resentful. What happens: The family sits in silence around the locked trunk after the funeral. Nobody speaks. Exactly 3 figures fully in the frame (Vikram, Savitri (Amma), Sunny); each appears only once; nobody else. Nobody looks into the camera lens: the camera is an invisible observer that nobody notices. Everyone is clearly Indian, with brown skin and Indian features, like real actors in an Indian TV serial; never cartoon, anime or plastic-looking.
